correctness.summary: Divide-and-conquer closest-pair never performs the strip merge step, so it always returns long.MaxValue regardless of input. The 'yt' strip array is filled but never used to compute any cross-strip distance, and the only distances ever compared come from recursion which bottoms out at long.MaxValue (the leaf case r-l<=1 returns MaxValue and never computes a pairwise distance).
correctness.triggeringInput: n=2, x=[0,1], y=[0,0] -> Run returns long.MaxValue; correct answer is 1. Same for any input (e.g. n=3 points (0,0),(3,0),(0,4) returns MaxValue instead of 9).
correctness.rootCause: Solve computes d = min(left,right) and builds the strip array yt[] (sorted-by-x order, not even sorted by y), but omits the entire merge: it never iterates the strip points comparing y-distances < d and never calls DistSq. The leaf/base case (r-l<=1) returns long.MaxValue without ever measuring the distance between two adjacent points, so no real distance ever enters the min.
correctness.suggestedFix: After computing d, run the standard strip check: for each pair of strip points (yt collected for those with (x[i]-mx)^2 < d) compare up to ~7 following points by squared y-distance, update d = min(d, DistSq(...)). Also ensure the base case actually computes the distance for the 2- and 3-point segments (e.g. brute force when r-l<=3). The strip must be merged in y-order to be correct/efficient.

perf.summary: Replace (ni+1)%n / (nj+1)%n with branch-free wrap to avoid a 64-bit integer division per caliper step.
perf.currentCost: Two `% n` operations per call inside the Run while-loop; n is arbitrary so Burst emits a full idiv (20-90 cycles each on the hot path), executed O(n) times.
perf.proposedChange: Compute next index with conditional increment: `int nni = ni + 1; if (nni == n) nni = 0;` (same for nnj). Indices are always in [0,n) and advance by exactly 1, so modulo is never needed.
perf.rationale: idiv is one of the most expensive integer ops; replacing it with a compare+cmov/branch removes a long-latency instruction from the inner caliper loop. Burst can turn the if into a branchless select.
perf.risk: None. ni,nj are seeded from FindExtremePoints in [0,n) and only ever incremented by these statements, so they stay in [0,n); +1 can reach at most n, handled by the == n reset.

perf.summary: Eliminate the three `% n` operations in the per-iteration calipers loop (ni, j advance, nj inside IsFurther) with conditional wraps.
perf.currentCost: `ni = (i+1)%n` once per outer iter, `j = (j+1)%n` per inner advance, and `nj = (j+1)%n` recomputed on every IsFurther call — all 64-bit idiv on arbitrary n.
perf.proposedChange: ni: `int ni = i + 1; if (ni == n) ni = 0;`. j advance: `int jn = j + 1; if (jn == n) jn = 0; j = jn;`. In IsFurther pass nj in or compute `nj = j + 1; if (nj == n) nj = 0;`. All values stay in [0,n).
perf.rationale: Removes idiv from both the outer loop and the inner while, the hottest part of the rotating-calipers scan, replacing each with a compare and conditional move.
perf.risk: None: every index is monotonically incremented by 1 from a value in [0,n), so the ==n reset is exactly equivalent to %n.

perf.summary: Avoid recomputing nj's wrap and redundant subtractions by hoisting; merge IsFurther's edge-vector computation with the loop.
perf.currentCost: IsFurther recomputes `(j+1)%n` and four subtractions every inner-loop probe; called repeatedly while advancing j.
perf.proposedChange: Track j's successor index incrementally alongside j in Run (advance both together), and pass the precomputed edge deltas, so IsFurther only does the cross product. Mark IsFurther AggressiveInlining.
perf.rationale: Shortens the dependency chain in the inner while and removes redundant modulo+subtract recomputation across consecutive probes.
perf.risk: None functionally; just reindexing. Keep cross-product sign test identical (>0).

perf.summary: Replace the two edge-delta precompute loops' `(k+1)%n` with a wrap-on-equal, and drop the resX/resY scratch buffers by writing directly to rx/ry.
perf.currentCost: `(k+1)%n1` and `(k+1)%n2` are idiv per edge in the two setup loops. Additionally resX/resY are stackalloc'd then copied to rx/ry in a final O(m) loop — 2*(n1+n2) longs of redundant stack and a full copy pass.
perf.proposedChange: For deltas use `int kn = k+1; if (kn==n1) kn=0;`. Write resX[m]/resY[m] directly into rx[m]/ry[m] throughout, removing resX/resY stackalloc and the final copy loop.
perf.rationale: Removes idiv from setup, eliminates 2*(n1+n2)*8 bytes of stack, and removes an entire O(m) copy pass plus its cache traffic. Output is written exactly once.
perf.risk: Caller supplies rx/ry sized >= n1+n2 (already required since m can reach n1+n2). Writing in-place is safe because rx/ry are distinct output buffers, not aliased with inputs. Edge wrap is exact since k ranges [0,n).

perf.summary: Solve builds the y-strip array yt but never compares strip points, so it returns only the min of the two halves and is both O(n) wasted work and arguably incorrect; the strip merge is missing.
perf.currentCost: The loop `for(i=l;i<r;i++) if((x[i]-mx)^2<d) yt[k++]=y[i];` fills yt but no pairwise distance over the strip is computed; result d is just min(left,right). Per node this is O(n) pure overhead with zero effect on the answer.
perf.proposedChange: Either (a) if the intent is a correct divide-and-conquer closest pair, sort/scan yt and check up to ~7 neighbors to fold strip distances into d; or (b) if behavior must be preserved as-is, delete the dead yt loop and the yt buffer entirely to reclaim n longs of stack and an O(n log n) pass.
perf.rationale: As written the strip loop is dead computation; removing it is a strict win. If correctness is desired, the standard 7-neighbor strip scan restores true O(n log n) closest-pair with the same asymptotics but a correct result.
perf.risk: Option (b) preserves current observable output exactly while removing work. Option (a) CHANGES output (fixes a likely bug) — only apply if the current result is known-wrong by design intent; flag for maintainer decision.

perf.summary: Insertion sort is O(n^2); for the closest-pair driver this dominates and defeats the divide-and-conquer's O(n log n) intent.
perf.currentCost: O(n^2) comparisons/moves to sort by x before Solve; on large n this is the bottleneck and a long dependency chain of shifts.
perf.proposedChange: Replace with an in-place O(n log n) sort over the parallel (sx,sy) arrays (e.g. heapsort or an iterative bottom-up mergesort using the existing yt buffer as scratch). Keep raw-pointer, no managed types.
perf.rationale: Drops the dominant cost from quadratic to n log n, matching the algorithm's intended complexity; especially important on mobile where large-n quadratic passes blow the cycle budget.
perf.risk: Must keep sx and sy permuted together identically. Heapsort avoids extra allocation; mergesort can reuse yt scratch. No semantic change to the sorted order (ascending x).
